title: Explaining Cause and Effect
objectives: Show relationships between events and outcomes
Use cause and effect language accurately

dialogue.title: Discussing a Traffic Problem
dialogue.context: Ahmed and coworkers discuss why they were late to work due to heavy traffic on the highway.

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.text: Good morning everyone. I noticed several people were late today. What happened?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Sorry we're late. There was terrible traffic on I-5. Because of an accident, all lanes were closed.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: Yes, that accident caused a huge backup. I was stuck for almost an hour.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: I heard on the radio that the accident happened early this morning during rush hour. That's why the traffic was so bad.

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.text: I see. Was anyone hurt in the accident?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: The news said a truck lost control due to wet roads. As a result, it hit several cars.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: The rain this morning made the roads slippery. Therefore, people should have driven more slowly.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: Exactly. Speeding in the rain is dangerous. This accident was probably preventable.

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.text: That's a good point. In the future, if there's bad weather, please leave earlier or let me know if you'll be delayed.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: That makes sense. Because we all take the same highway, maybe we should carpool on rainy days. That way, if one of us is stuck, at least fewer people are late.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: Great idea! Carpooling would also save money on gas and help the environment.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: Plus, we can use the carpool lane, which moves faster during rush hour. That's a win-win situation.

examples: I was late because there was traffic.
She stayed home because she was sick.
They moved because of better job opportunities.
We canceled the picnic because it rained.
He's tired because he didn't sleep well.

pattern_drills.focus: Showing result with 'therefore' and 'as a result'
examples: It rained heavily. Therefore, the game was canceled.
She studied hard. As a result, she passed the test.
The store closed early. Therefore, we couldn't shop.
He missed the bus. As a result, he was late.
The roads were icy. Therefore, schools were closed.
The weather was bad. That's why we stayed home.
She loves animals. That's why she became a vet.
Gas prices increased. That's why I take the bus now.
The restaurant was full. That's why we waited an hour.
He speaks three languages. That's why he got the job.

listening_exercises.transcript: Cause and effect relationships are everywhere. A cause is why something happens. An effect is what happens as a result. For example: Cause - It rained for three days. Effect - The river flooded. Understanding cause and effect helps you explain situations, solve problems, and make predictions about what might happen next.
listening_exercises.question: What is a cause?

listening_exercises.transcript: Common cause words: because, since, due to, because of, as a result of. Common effect words: therefore, so, consequently, as a result, thus. Choose words carefully: 'because' and 'since' are followed by clauses with subjects and verbs. 'Due to' and 'because of' are followed by noun phrases. For example: 'Because it rained' versus 'Due to the rain.'
listening_exercises.question: What follows 'because'?
options: A clause with subject and verb

listening_exercises.transcript: Multiple causes can lead to one effect, and one cause can have multiple effects. For example: The company failed because of poor management, high costs, and increased competition (multiple causes, one effect). The pandemic caused business closures, job losses, and remote work (one cause, multiple effects). Recognizing complex cause-effect relationships helps you understand real-world situations.
listening_exercises.question: Can one effect have multiple causes?

speaking_tasks.prompt: Explain why you made an important decision (moving to a new place, changing jobs, etc.). Use cause and effect language. Record for 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: I decided to move to America because I wanted better opportunities for my family. In my country, jobs were scarce and the economy was struggling. As a result, I couldn't save money or plan for the future. That's why I applied for immigration. The process took three years due to long waiting times. When I finally arrived, I was nervous but hopeful. Because of this move, my children will have access to good education and healthcare. It was a difficult decision, but I believe the long-term effects will be positive for my entire family.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Describe a problem in your community and explain what caused it. Then suggest a solution. Record for 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: In my neighborhood, there's a serious parking problem. Because the apartment building has more residents than parking spaces, people park on the street illegally. This causes conflicts between neighbors. The problem exists because the building was built 40 years ago when fewer people had cars. As a result, they didn't plan for enough parking. Therefore, I think the solution is to rent spaces in a nearby lot or create a parking rotation schedule. If we work together, we can solve this issue peacefully.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write about a change in your life. Explain the cause (why it happened) and the effects (what resulted from it). Use cause-effect language. (80-100 words)
writing_tasks.example: Learning English has completely changed my life. I decided to study English because I needed it for work and daily communication in America. This decision required a lot of time and effort. As a result, I had less free time for other activities. However, the positive effects have been enormous. Because I can speak English better now, I got a promotion at work. I've also made American friends, which has helped me understand the culture better. Therefore, my overall quality of life has improved significantly. Due to these positive outcomes, I continue to study English every day. That's why I believe learning a new language is one of the best investments you can make.

writing_tasks.prompt: Choose a current event or social issue. Explain what caused it and what effects it's having. (70-90 words)
writing_tasks.example: Climate change is one of the most serious issues facing the world. It's caused by multiple factors, including burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrial pollution. Because of increased carbon emissions, global temperatures are rising. As a result, we're seeing more extreme weather events like hurricanes, droughts, and wildfires. These changes are affecting agriculture, causing crop failures in some regions. Therefore, food prices are increasing. The effects are also visible in ocean levels rising, which threatens coastal cities. That's why many scientists say we need to take immediate action to reduce emissions.

grammar_focus.title: 'Because' and 'Since' for Cause
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'because' or 'since' to introduce the reason or cause. Both are followed by subject + verb.
examples: I was late because there was traffic. (cause)
Since it was raining, we stayed inside. (cause)
She's tired because she worked all night. (cause)
Since he's busy, I'll call him later. (cause)

practice.sentence: I stayed home ___ I was sick.
They left early because they ___ tired.

grammar_focus.title: 'So' and 'Therefore' for Effect
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'so' or 'therefore' to show result or effect.
examples: It rained, so we canceled the picnic. (effect)
She studied hard. Therefore, she passed. (effect)
He was tired, so he went to bed early. (effect)
The store closed. Therefore, we left. (effect)

practice.sentence: It was late, ___ we went home.
He missed the bus. ___, he was late.
She's sick, so she ___ go to work.

grammar_focus.title: Conditionals for Cause-Effect Predictions
examples: If it rains, the game will be canceled. (prediction)
If you study, you'll pass the test. (predicted effect)
If we leave now, we'll arrive on time. (predicted outcome)
If she's late, we'll start without her. (planned consequence)

practice.sentence: If it rains, we ___ stay inside.

questions.question: Why were people late to work?
What caused the accident?
options: A truck lost control on wet roads

questions.question: Complete: 'I was late ___ there was traffic.'
'Because' is followed by a clause with subject and verb.
One cause can only have one effect.
It rained. ___, the game was canceled. (showing effect)
If it rains, we ___ stay inside. (conditional prediction)
What word shows result or effect?

vocabulary.example: The cause of the fire was faulty wiring.
The effect of the rain was flooding.
As a result, we were late.
The consequence of speeding is danger.
Due to rain, we stayed home.
The decision had a big impact.

cultural_notes: In American business culture, explaining cause and effect clearly is highly valued. It shows logical thinking.
When explaining why you're late or made a mistake, Americans appreciate taking responsibility rather than making excuses.
In academic settings, cause-effect analysis is fundamental to science, history, and social studies.
Americans value problem-solving skills, which require understanding cause-effect relationships.
News media often use cause-effect language to explain events: 'The storm caused power outages affecting 10,000 homes.'
In professional writing, using phrases like 'therefore' and 'as a result' makes your arguments more persuasive.
